title: Stop scrambling your propeller: MOZA AB6 analog brake setup guide
description:
For years, experiencing true mechanical Force Feedback (FFB) in flight simulation meant either spending a fortune on high-end commercial gear or spending dozens of hours building a complex DIY rig. The brand-new Moza Flight AB6 bundle completely changes the landscape. Combining a full-metal, 6 Newton-meter peak torque dual-servo base with a carbon-fiber-reinforced flight stick, this system aims to bring genuine haptic control loading down to an accessible consumer price tier.

In this deep-dive hardware guide, we bypass the marketing scripts to look at a massive hardware problem with this fighter-style bundle and the ingenious secret weapon hidden right on the metal base that completely fixes it for both Flight Simulator 2020 and 2024. Because the bundled MHG grip lacks an analog handbrake lever, trying to taxi a taildragger using digital button binds is a recipe for a ground loop or a prop strike. We look closer at the AB6 base panel to leverage its built-in sliders as a mini button box, bringing smooth, fractional braking to your vintage warbirds and GA aircraft.

We walk step-by-step through the MOZA Cockpit utility to set your sliders to axis mode and calibrate them from 0 to 100%. Finally, we load into Microsoft Flight Simulator to clear out the default digital binds and map a perfectly graduated left and right differential braking profile that keeps your tail on the tarmac.
